complete_examples.text: In the past decades, an interesting question was put forward by Zeng et al. [22], that is, the equations of motion built in Refs. [2–10,18–21] have not satisfied two fundamental conditions at the wheel–rail interface in essence: (I) displacement compatibility; (II) force equilibrium.

Conclusions In this paper, a comprehensive work is devoted to build a 3D model for vehicle–track interactions, in which an emphasis is paid on constructing a dynamic model where the displacement compatibility and force equilibrium between the vehicle and the tracks, moreover, considering the complex wheel–rail contact geometries.

The train and the bridge are coupled as an entire one through geometrical complementarity and force equilibrium at wheel-rail interfaces [10], the methods like Lagrange multiplier [11], Guyan reduction scheme [12], dynamic condensation method [13] and energy principle [14,15], etc.

The system excitations are originated from the wheel/rail interactions by track geometries instead of moving loads, most importantly, the wheel/rail displacement complementarity and force equilibrium are satisfied in matrix characterizations, and accordingly arbitrary time steps can be implemented with a guarantee of computational stability.
The displacement compatibility and force equilibrium are automat ically satisfied between the motions of subsystems in Equation (16).

First, a coupled model, with the satisfaction of wheel–rail displacement compatibility and force equilibrium within each time step, is constructed for the characterisation of vehicle–track interaction, where the vehicle is modelled as a multi-rigid-body system, the ballasted tracks are modelled as a combination of elasticity, damping and mass structures by finite-element method, and time-varying wheel–rail contacts in geometry, creep and force are depicted at the three-dimensional space.
In this way, the vehicle and the tracks can be solved with wheel–rail displacement compatibility and force equilibrium satisfied.
In multibody dynamics based on force-equilibrium methods, Hertzian contact and creep theories have been applied in vehicle–track model constructions.
In equation (17), it can be observed that vehicle and the tracks are wholly coupled as an entire system no matter on displacement complementarity and on force equilibrium.
For modelling train– track interaction, a matrix representation method is developed to depict the displacement compatibility and force equilibrium between the train and tracks.
